sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `prime-agent`. [claim-prime-agent-product-identity]
- Canonical name: Prime Agent, maintained by Prime Intellect in the canonical repository. [claim-prime-agent-product-identity] [claim-prime-agent-vendor]
- Current status: the repository was public and non-archived, and v0.7.1 was the latest stable release dated 2026-08-07. [claim-prime-agent-repository-status] [claim-prime-agent-version]
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-09. [claim-prime-agent-product-identity]

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Prime Intellect describes Prime Agent as an open-source terminal coding and research agent for general and long-running work. [claim-prime-agent-product-identity] [claim-prime-agent-what-it-is]
- What it is not: checked sources establish a local runtime and daemon boundary, not a proven vendor-hosted cloud agent or remote control plane. [claim-prime-agent-what-it-is-not]

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a project-taxonomy inference from model, tool, context, and session ownership. [claim-prime-agent-primary-type-runtime]
- Agent-loop owner: the TypeScript host and `AgentSession` own provider calls and lifecycle; persistent IPython is the model-facing control environment. [claim-prime-agent-agent-loop-owner]
- Architecture: terminal client, local daemon, worker, root/child sessions, IPython kernel, JSONL/artifact storage, and selected providers are separate layers. [claim-prime-agent-architecture]

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-cli`, `surface-prime-agent-print`, `surface-prime-agent-json`, `surface-prime-agent-rpc`, `surface-prime-agent-acp`, `surface-prime-agent-sdk`, `surface-prime-agent-termux`, and `surface-prime-agent-windows`. [claim-prime-agent-surface-cli] [claim-prime-agent-surface-print] [claim-prime-agent-json] [claim-prime-agent-rpc] [claim-prime-agent-acp] [claim-prime-agent-sdk] [claim-prime-agent-surface-termux] [claim-prime-agent-surface-windows]
- Execution location: tools and local workers run in the current project on the user's machine; model calls go to the selected provider. [claim-prime-agent-local-execution]

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: a built-in catalog, interactive/CLI model selection, custom models, and local compatible endpoints are documented. [claim-prime-agent-model-strategy]
- Auth strategy: subscription OAuth, CLI keys, local `~/.prime/agent/auth.json`, environment variables, custom providers, and a Prime Inference-specific path are documented. [claim-prime-agent-auth-strategy]
- Provider support: provider docs cover subscription, direct API, cloud/gateway, `models.json`, and local Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM routes; extension docs separately cover custom endpoints, proxies, OAuth/SSO flows, and custom streaming APIs. [claim-prime-agent-provider-support] [claim-prime-agent-model-strategy] [claim-prime-agent-custom-providers]

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: the vendor's RLM design treats context as a variable in persistent Python and delegates selected work to child model calls. [claim-prime-agent-context-behavior]
- Memory: Continual Harness state can persist prompt notes, memories, skills, subagent specs, and refinement events. [claim-prime-agent-memory]
- Compaction: automatic/manual compaction and branch summaries are documented; kernel restoration is best effort for non-serializable objects. [claim-prime-agent-compaction]
- Session behavior: JSONL persistence supports resume, ephemeral opt-out, tree navigation, fork, clone, and branch summaries. [claim-prime-agent-session-persistence] [claim-prime-agent-session-branching]

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: the default model-facing tool is persistent IPython, with project shell commands available through Python-cell composition. [claim-prime-agent-tools]
- Extensions: trusted TypeScript extensions can add tools, commands, providers, UI, events, and compaction behavior. [claim-prime-agent-extensions]
- MCP: HTTP MCP is exposed through Python-backed skills; stdio MCP is not wired to the kernel. [claim-prime-agent-mcp]
- Skills: Agent Skills markdown and Python-backed skills are documented. [claim-prime-agent-skills]
- Hooks: extensions can intercept tools/results, block actions, inject context, and customize compaction or sessions. [claim-prime-agent-hooks]
- APIs: in-process SDK, JSONL RPC, JSON event stream, and local ACP process modes are documented. [claim-prime-agent-sdk] [claim-prime-agent-rpc] [claim-prime-agent-json] [claim-prime-agent-acp]

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: recursive children, agent messaging, harness updates, goals, schedules, heartbeats, and bounded autonomous continuations support an inferred secondary orchestration role. [claim-prime-agent-orchestration] [claim-prime-agent-secondary-role-orchestrator]
- Parallelism: independent child runtimes can run concurrently, while ordinary cells serialize within one kernel. [claim-prime-agent-parallelism]

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: workers and kernels use separate processes for lifecycle containment, but this is not a security sandbox. [claim-prime-agent-process-isolation]
- Permissions: model Python, project commands, extensions, and skills run with worker/user OS permissions; default approval-action behavior remains unknown. [claim-prime-agent-permission-boundary] [claim-prime-agent-default-approval-unknown]
- Security: local auth uses owner-only permissions and locking; the host retains credentials, and pseudonymous telemetry excludes the listed content fields. [claim-prime-agent-auth-file-security] [claim-prime-agent-credential-boundary] [claim-prime-agent-telemetry]
- Data path: default JSONL sessions and artifacts stay under `~/.prime/agent`; auth stays at `~/.prime/agent/auth.json`, and provider requests go to the configured endpoint. [claim-prime-agent-data-path] [claim-prime-agent-auth-strategy] [claim-prime-agent-local-execution]

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-cli` is the local interactive TUI/CLI with tool inspection and daemon-backed local continuity. [claim-prime-agent-surface-cli]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-print` is local headless CLI mode. [claim-prime-agent-surface-print]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-json`, `surface-prime-agent-rpc`, `surface-prime-agent-acp`, and `surface-prime-agent-sdk` are local integration surfaces, not hosted APIs. [claim-prime-agent-json] [claim-prime-agent-rpc] [claim-prime-agent-acp] [claim-prime-agent-sdk]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-termux` is same-device Android terminal use, not native mobile. [claim-prime-agent-surface-termux]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-prime-agent-windows` is a same-device Windows CLI route requiring bash. [claim-prime-agent-surface-windows]
- Remote behavior: first-party remote client, vendor relay, remote start, and remote resume remain unknown; generic SSH or private networking is not credited as product support. [claim-prime-agent-remote-access-unknown] [claim-prime-agent-vendor-relay-unknown]
- Mobile behavior: Termux is documented; native iOS/Android graphical, first-party mobile web, and user messaging gateways remain unknown. [claim-prime-agent-surface-termux] [claim-prime-agent-mobile-access-unknown] [claim-prime-agent-messaging-access-unknown]
- Background behavior: resident local daemon workers support detach/reattach, schedules, heartbeats, and bounded autonomous continuation. [claim-prime-agent-background-sessions] [claim-prime-agent-scheduling] [claim-prime-agent-autonomous-goals]

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: standalone Prime Agent software pricing is unknown; provider-specific subscription and API billing remain separate. [claim-prime-agent-pricing-unknown] [claim-prime-agent-provider-costs]
- License: MIT. [claim-prime-agent-license-mit]
- Maintenance: the release endpoint recorded v0.7.1 on 2026-08-07; repository metadata separately recorded a 2026-08-09 push. [claim-prime-agent-maintenance-signal] [claim-prime-agent-repository-status]
- Lock-in: an inference finds reduced single-provider dependence but product-specific session, artifact, extension, skill, and harness state. [claim-prime-agent-lock-in]

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: current docs call the origin a hard fork of `pi-mono` and describe current Prime Agent development/distribution as independent. [claim-prime-agent-pi-origin] [claim-prime-agent-independent-lineage] Current README header still links `badlogic/pi-mono`; Acknowledgements name `earendil-works/pi`. [claim-prime-agent-sf-readme-cites-both-slugs]
- Relationship edges: the existing baseline tuple remains `prime-agent --built_on--> pi`; no duplicate `built_on` or new `fork_of` tuple is proposed. [claim-prime-agent-pi-origin]

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `neighborhood-pi-lineage-terminal-runtimes`. [claim-prime-agent-lineage-neighborhood]
- Substitutes: unknown; lineage does not prove equivalent operating models. [claim-prime-agent-lineage-neighborhood]
- Partial substitutes: unknown pending same-user-job evidence beyond lineage. [claim-prime-agent-lineage-neighborhood]
- Same-lineage relatives: Pi, Atomic, and Oh My Pi; Prime Agent's decisive differences are RLM/IPython control, Continual Harness state, resident daemon workers, schedules, and goals. [claim-prime-agent-lineage-neighborhood] [claim-prime-agent-unique-value]
- Often-confused products: hosted cloud agents and remote control planes are not established as Prime Agent's product type. [claim-prime-agent-what-it-is-not]
- Complements: unknown within an eligible Wave 1 comparison neighborhood. [claim-prime-agent-lineage-neighborhood]

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: Prime Intellect positions the product around persistent RLM Python control plus a self-refining Continual Harness. [claim-prime-agent-unique-value]
- Meaningful drawbacks: no built-in security sandbox, and current MCP integration does not wire stdio servers into the kernel. [claim-prime-agent-no-sandbox-drawback] [claim-prime-agent-mcp-stdio-drawback]
- Best fit: vendor positioning targets coding, long-horizon evaluation, research, and autoresearch. [claim-prime-agent-intended-user]
- Not-for: an inference excludes untrusted work without external isolation and use cases that require verified native mobile, messaging, relay, or first-party remote clients. [claim-prime-agent-not-for]
